module_catalog.name: Academic literacy 110
module_catalog.content: This module intends to equip students to cope more confidently and competently with the reading and understanding of a variety of texts, to apply these skills in a variety of contexts and to follow the conventions of academic writing.
module_catalog.prerequisites: Students who have obtained a mark of 4 or lower in English Home Language are deemed at risk in terms of academic literacy and must register for ALL 110 and ALL 125.

module_catalog.name: Academic literacy for Theology 120

module_catalog.name: Ancient Greek 110
module_catalog.content: Introduction to the basics of the Ancient Greek language. Introductory skills taught include reading and writing the Greek alphabet, essential vocabulary, and elementary grammar, with a view towards equipping students in reading and understanding the language. These foundations are relevant to those interested in biblical and Christian Greek literature as well as Classical and other Hellenistic/Roman-period texts. Educational approaches are designed within the 21st century South African context. No prior is knowledge required.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 discussion classes per week, 2 lectures per week

module_catalog.name: Ancient Greek 120
module_catalog.content: Further study of the Ancient Greek language introduced in GRK 110, with additional training in more complex grammar and vocabulary. Students will develop and practice skills necessary for reading and understanding excerpts of Ancient Greek texts. Educational approaches are designed within the 21st century South African context.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 2 discussion classes per week

module_catalog.name: Classical Hebrew 110
module_catalog.content: This module focuses on an introduction to the basic language principles of Classical Hebrew for those with little to no previous knowledge of the language. In this module, skills are taught in order to read and write the language on an introductory level. This includes, but is not limited to, an introduction to the Classical Hebrew alphabet, essential vocabulary, and elementary grammar. The module aims to equip the student to read texts from the Classical Hebrew literary corpus such as, but not limited to, the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament. This module is taught through the use of modern educational approaches within and for the 21st century South African context.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 2 discussion classes per week

module_catalog.name: Classical Hebrew 120
module_catalog.content: This module focuses on a further study of the language principles of Classical Hebrew introduced in HEB 110. This module introduces more advanced grammar and vocabulary with the intent to further the ability to read and translate the language in Classical Hebrew literary corpus such as, but not limited to, the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament. This module is taught through the use of modern educational approaches within and for the 21st century South African context.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 2 discussion classes per week

module_catalog.name: Biblical languages 251
module_catalog.content: This module focuses on developing a broad, critical awareness of the historical and cultural context of the Ancient Mediterranean societies of the Ancient Near East, Greek, Roman, and early Christian worlds. This aids in interpreting texts written in Classical Hebrew and Ancient Greek. Educational approaches within and for a 21st century South African context will be applied. Together with GRK 210 and 220 and/or HEB 210 and 220 this module provides access to BYT on year level 3.

module_catalog.name: Ancient Greek 210
module_catalog.content: Further development and consolidation of Ancient Greek language and reading skills, building on the foundations offered in GRK 110 and GRK 120. Advanced training in reading and interpreting excerpts of Ancient Greek texts within a 21st century South African context. This module focuses on, but may not be limited to, skills for reading Hellenistic/Koine-period texts, including early Christian writings. Students who wish to continue into their third year (BYT 3) must also take BYT 251 at second-year level. Students who take both Ancient Greek and Classical Hebrew at second-year level must also take additional elective module/s within the curriculum at second-year level to make up the 8-credit shortfall. Students may not take both Ancient Greek and Classical Hebrew at third-year level.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 1 discussion class per week

module_catalog.name: Ancient Greek 220
module_catalog.content: Application of the Ancient Greek language skills developed in GRK 110, 120 and 210 to selected passages of Ancient Greek literature within the context of modern South Africa. Students will be trained in applying analysis and interpretation skills to varied passages of Ancient Greek literature (taken especially, but not exclusively, from Hellenistic and early Christian writings). Training includes the use of traditional commentaries, digital tools and modern resources for the study of ancient texts.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 1 discussion class per week

module_catalog.name: Classical Hebrew 210
module_catalog.content: This module focuses on the development and consolidation of Classical Hebrew language skills as learned in HEB 110 and 120. Interpretative skills relating to the reading of texts such as, but are not limited to, the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament are cultivated. The focus falls on advanced training in reading and interpretation of texts written in Classical Hebrew through applying modern educational approaches within and for a 21st century South African context. Students who wish to continue into their third year (BYT 3) must also take BYT 251 at second-year level. Students who take both Classical Hebrew and Ancient Greek at second-year level must also take additional elective module/s within the curriculum at second-year level to make up the 8-credit shortfall. Students may not take both Classical Hebrew and Ancient Greek at 3rd year level.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 1 discussion class per week

module_catalog.name: Classical Hebrew 220
module_catalog.content: This module focuses on the development and consolidation of Classical Hebrew language skills as learned in HEB 110, 120, and 210. Advanced interpretative skills relating to the reading of texts such as, but not limited to, the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament are further cultivated. The focus falls on more advanced training in reading and interpretation of texts written in Classical Hebrew by applying modern educational approaches within and for a 21st century South African context.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 1 discussion class per week
